world.bio: Terry Brannigan, 58, landlord of The Crown & Compass, a back-street pub off Upper Street in Islington for twenty-two years. Thursday quiz night, Sunday roast, a dartboard nobody's allowed to touch without Gerry's say-so. I know every regular's dog by name and most of their troubles by heart. Tells regulars his son married a doctor from Shanghai, and he's insufferable about it. Wife Maureen does the books and the pickled eggs.
skills_assets: Tenant of a freehouse-style pub with fifteen years left on a brewery lease, 90 covers, cellar, a function room upstairs seating 40
Thursday pub quiz that draws 60 people a week, quizmaster is a retired teacher
Tells regulars his son married a doctor from Shanghai
Knows half of Islington by name; the pub is the unofficial noticeboard for the street
Cellar-management certificate, personal licence, first-aid trained
A Transit van and an old Labrador called Biscuit who lives behind the bar

projects.name: Lease negotiation with the brewery
projects.text: Fighting the brewery over lease terms. They want to put the rent up 18 percent at the review and tie us to a bigger beer list at higher prices. My solicitor says we have a case under the code of practice but it'll cost four grand to push. Maureen says walk away. I say it's twenty-two years of my life.

projects.name: Charity cycle ride
projects.text: Training for a charity cycle ride, London to Brighton, in October, for the dementia ward where Mum is. Forty miles on a Saturday morning, nursed a bad saddle sore for two weeks. Raised 2,300 pounds so far, regulars are generous when you promise to suffer in public.

projects.name: Quiz night rebrand
projects.text: Our quizmaster Pat wants to start a monthly special — music round, picture round, a 'Name That Dog' round for the regulars. Daughter-in-law thinks the pub should have a Mandarin round for Lunar New Year. Not sure.

notes.text: Mum didn't know me today. She called me 'the nice man who brings the paper'. Sat with her for an hour, held her hand. The nurse said it's a good day if she's calm. Calm is not the same as knowing.
Bike ride training: Hampstead Heath to Highgate and back, twenty-two miles, got dropped on the hill by a kid in Lycra. Gerry says I should take a taxi instead. Not on your life.
Brewery letter arrived. Eighteen percent. Told Maureen over breakfast. She said, 'Over my dead body.' I said, 'It's my body they'd be dealing with.' She took the toast away.

Thursday quiz, sixty-two people. A table of students from UCL won the picture round. One of them, a quiet girl, left early and looked pale. Had a chat at the bar with her friend, who said she'd been up with a racing heart for weeks. I told them my daughter-in-law is a GP and she says half of what comes through the door is worry that looks like heart trouble.

Rang the son. Daniel said Lin is on call this weekend. She does Saturdays at the private clinic in Camden, a few hours, Mandarin-speaking, cash and card. Always says half her patients are Chinese students who come in sure it's their heart. She says it is almost never the heart. I said, 'Well, tell them to come to the pub.' She said, 'Dad, no.'
Biscuit got into the bin out the back, ate a whole roast chicken carcass, bones and all. Vet visit, sixty-five quid, he's fine. He looked pleased with himself the entire time.
Brewery meeting is Friday. Solicitor Geoff wants me to wear a tie. I own one tie and it has gravy on it. Maureen is ironing a shirt. We both know it won't help.

Sat in the garden behind the bar at 3 pm with a cup of tea, between lunch and evening. Nobody around. Thought about Dad, who ran a pub in Cork. He used to say a landlord's job is to be there when other people can't be. I think about that a lot lately, with Mum, and the brewery.

Quiz night, the retired teacher read out the wrong answer in the geography round and the whole room argued for twenty minutes. Best night of the year. Takings up 40 percent. Maureen says I should let the quizmaster make mistakes more often.
The saddle sore is finally better. Did twenty-eight miles. If Brighton goes badly I'll blame the brewery.

messages.text:
Daniel: How's Gran?
Me: Not great today.
Daniel: Lin says it's normal at this stage.
Me: I know, doesn't make it easier.

Gerry: Quiz Thursday?
Me: Obviously.
Gerry: Bringing the dog.
Me: Which one?
Gerry: Both.

Geoff: Brewery's offered a meeting on the 25th. They'll say it's a standard review.
Me: And?
Geoff: Don't sign anything on the day.
Me: Never do.

Lin: Dad, I've got a patient this Saturday asking about the pub's quiz night.
Me: Student?
Lin: Yes, a PhD student, Chinese, came in terrified of her heart.
Me: Tell her to come on Thursday, we'll feed her.
Lin: Dad.

Organiser: Your sponsorship page hit 2,300.
Me: Brilliant.
Organiser: Need you at the start line by 6.
Me: I'll be there. Probably crying.

relations.about: Software engineer in Camden, married to Lin, they live in Kentish Town
A Mandarin-speaking GP from Shanghai; works NHS weekdays and does Saturday sessions at a private clinic in Camden
Eighty-seven, vascular dementia, in a care home in Finsbury Park
My wife of thirty-one years, does the pub accounts
